title: Immutability of God
definition: The immutability of God means that God does not change in His being, character, purposes, promises, or faithfulness.
summary: God is unchanging, steady, faithful, and true.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals the unchanging faithfulness of God and remains the same yesterday, today, and forever.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God's immutability means He is not unstable, moody, improving, declining, or surprised into change. His character remains perfect, His promises remain reliable, and His purposes stand.

This does not mean God is inactive or impersonal. He truly acts in history, answers prayer, judges, saves, comforts, and restores. But He does so without becoming less than who He eternally is.

The unchanging God is a refuge for changing people. In Christ, believers see that God's saving mercy and covenant faithfulness are secure.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People are often shaped by unstable relationships, changing circumstances, and broken promises. The immutability of God matters because it gives believers a firm place to stand.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Anchor your confidence in God's unchanging character. When emotions shift or circumstances shake, return to what Scripture says God has always been and will always be.
